name: Specter Desktop
description: Electron wrapper downloads+executes specterd; SHA256 baked into the bundled manifest (pinned-at-build hash, no signature).
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Specter Desktop’s wrapper checks its specterd component against an architecture-specific SHA-256 value bundled in version data. This supports a component-integrity observation; the complete release-authentication policy remains unestablished.
limitations: Newly retrieved default-branch snapshot, not historical release re-verification; the provenance and delivery of version-data.json and external GitHub release controls were not independently audited.

original_evidence.text: | Specter Desktop | github.com/cryptoadvance/specter-desktop | Python/Flask backend + Electron desktop wrapper (pyinstaller/electron) | N (no mechanism checks a remote server for a *newer* app version; no electron-updater/autoUpdater present) | N/A for self-update — however at first run/repair the Electron wrapper unconditionally downloads the "specterd" companion daemon binary matching the version already pinned in the shipped app bundle | Y (downloads `specterd-<version>-<platform>.zip` from GitHub Releases, extracts it, and executes it as the backend daemon) | https (github.com/.../releases/download/... via Node `request` lib, standard TLS/OS trust store, no pinning) | N (`version-data.json` is a plain JSON file bundled inside the app package at build time by `set-version.js`; it is not independently/detachedly signed) | hash-from-manifest (downloaded specterd's SHA-256 is compared against the hash baked into the bundled `version-data.json`) | none (hash only, no signature/key; the manifest's own integrity rests solely on the outer Electron app package's code signing, e.g. mac "identity": "Kim Neunert" in electron-builder config, not on any key checked by this download logic) | pyinstaller/electron/downloadloc.js:1-14 (GitHub releases URL builder); pyinstaller/electron/src/download.js:31-78 (download→extract→SHA256 compare→execute); pyinstaller/electron/set-version.js:1-59 (hash baked into version-data.json at build time) |

fields.label: has_updater
fields.value: N (no mechanism checks a remote server for a *newer* app version; no electron-updater/autoUpdater present)

fields.label: auto
fields.value: N/A for self-update — however at first run/repair the Electron wrapper unconditionally downloads the "specterd" companion daemon binary matching the version already pinned in the shipped app bundle

fields.label: downloads_and_executes
fields.value: Y (downloads `specterd-<version>-<platform>.zip` from GitHub Releases, extracts it, and executes it as the backend daemon)

fields.label: transport
fields.value: https (github.com/.../releases/download/... via Node `request` lib, standard TLS/OS trust store, no pinning)

fields.label: manifest_signed
fields.value: N (`version-data.json` is a plain JSON file bundled inside the app package at build time by `set-version.js`; it is not independently/detachedly signed)

fields.label: payload_verification
fields.value: hash-from-manifest (downloaded specterd's SHA-256 is compared against the hash baked into the bundled `version-data.json`)

fields.label: verifying_key_source
fields.value: none (hash only, no signature/key; the manifest's own integrity rests solely on the outer Electron app package's code signing, e.g. mac "identity": "Kim Neunert" in electron-builder config, not on any key checked by this download logic)

fields.label: evidence
fields.value: pyinstaller/electron/downloadloc.js:1-14 (GitHub releases URL builder); pyinstaller/electron/src/download.js:31-78 (download→extract→SHA256 compare→execute); pyinstaller/electron/set-version.js:1-59 (hash baked into version-data.json at build time)
